title: Why You’re Always Overwhelmed | The Psychology of Priorities & Procrastination

sentences.en: Psychologists, what if you could earn money beyond trading your time for money?
sentences.zh: 心理学家们，如果你们能通过出卖时间赚钱之外还能获得收益，会怎么样？

sentences.en: I'm Dr. Marianne Trent, clinical psychologist, and I've been developing passive and recurring income streams since 2019.
sentences.zh: 我是临床心理学家玛丽安·特伦特博士，自2019年以来，我一直在开发被动和循环收入来源。

sentences.en: I have some exciting news.
sentences.zh: 我有个好消息要告诉大家。

sentences.en: Sophie Foote's One-to-Many program is now open for enrollment.
sentences.zh: 苏菲·富特的“一对多”项目现已开放报名。

sentences.en: It's designed to help you turn your expertise into scalable offers like courses, memberships, and digital products.
sentences.zh: 它旨在帮助你将专业知识转化为可扩展的产品，如课程、会员资格和数字产品。

sentences.en: I completed the program myself in 2022 and have since supported two cohorts of psychologists through their journeys too.
sentences.zh: 我自己于2022年完成了这个项目，此后也一直支持两期心理学家完成他们的旅程。

sentences.en: And if you join through my affiliate link, you'll receive Sophie's bonuses plus my own exclusive support package at no extra coSt.
sentences.zh: 如果你通过我的联盟链接加入，你将获得苏菲的奖金以及我独家的专属支持套餐，不收取额外费用。

sentences.en: That includes six months of WhatsApp support, four group masterminds, masterclasses, personalized guidance, a Fortnum and Mason treat, and a time-limited one-to-one coaching bonus.
sentences.zh: 这包括六个月的WhatsApp支持、四场小组头脑风暴大师课、大师班、个性化指导、一份福特南与梅森的慰问品以及限时的一对一教练指导奖金。

sentences.en: Enrollment closes on Monday the 16th of November at 10pm.
sentences.zh: 报名将于11月16日星期一晚上10点截止。

sentences.en: Find out more via my bonus page linked in the description.
sentences.zh: 通过简介中链接的我的福利页面了解更多信息。

sentences.en: And remember, you must purchase through my link to receive my bonuses.
sentences.zh: 请记住，你必须通过我的链接购买才能获得我的福利。

sentences.en: I'm here if you have any questions.
sentences.zh: 如果你有任何问题，我随时都在。

sentences.en: Netflix once said their biggest competitor was sleep.
sentences.zh: 网飞曾说过，他们最大的竞争对手是睡眠。

sentences.en: And honestly, that tells you everything about modern life.
sentences.zh: 说实话，这说明了现代生活的一切。

sentences.en: We live in a world where everything feels important all the time.
sentences.zh: 我们生活在一个所有事情在任何时候都显得很重要的世界里。

sentences.en: Every email, every opinion, every task, every notification competing for our attention.
sentences.zh: 每一封电子邮件、每一个观点、每一项任务、每一个通知都在争夺我们的注意力。

sentences.en: And in the middle of all that, a lot of people have completely lost sight of what actually matters to them.
sentences.zh: 而在这一切的中心，许多人已经完全忽视了对他们真正重要的事情。

sentences.en: So in this episode, author Lily Silverton and I explore procrastination, comparison, overwhelm attention, and why modern life makes it so hard to prioritize ourselves.
sentences.zh: 因此，在这一期节目中，我和作家莉莉·西尔弗顿将探讨拖延、比较、不知所措的注意力，以及为什么现代生活让我们如此难以优先关注自己。

sentences.en: I hope you find it really useful.
sentences.zh: 希望你觉得这真的很有用。

sentences.en: If you do, like and subscribe for more.
sentences.zh: 如果你觉得有用，请点赞并订阅以获取更多内容。

sentences.en: Hi, welcome to Psychology Actually.
sentences.zh: 嗨，欢迎来到“心理学其实很简单”。

sentences.en: I'm Dr. Marianne Trent, a qualified clinical psychologiSt.
sentences.zh: 我是玛丽安·特伦特博士，一名合格的临床心理学家。

sentences.en: And we are welcoming our guest today for today's episode.
sentences.zh: 今天我们要迎来本期节目的嘉宾。

sentences.en: Lily Silverton, author of Prioritize This.
sentences.zh: 莉莉·西尔弗顿，《优先考虑》一书的作者。

sentences.en: Welcome, Lily.
sentences.zh: 欢迎你，莉莉。

sentences.en: Hi, Marianne.
sentences.zh: 嗨，玛丽安。

sentences.en: Thank you for having me.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你邀请我。

sentences.en: Thank you for being here.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你能来。

sentences.en: So tell us a little bit about why prioritizing anything is a good idea, Lily.
sentences.zh: 那么，莉莉，跟我们讲讲为什么把任何事情放在优先地位都是个好主意吧。

sentences.en: Well, we, I think, as you very well know, particularly within your work, we live in a very demanding world.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我想，正如你非常清楚的那样，尤其是在你的工作中，我们生活在一个要求很高的世界里。

sentences.en: We have very demanding lives externally.
sentences.zh: 我们在外部生活中有很高的要求。

sentences.en: We have very demanding lives internally in terms of what's going on in our psyches.
sentences.zh: 就我们的心理活动而言，我们在内部生活中也有很高的要求。

sentences.en: And we can be made to feel and we can make ourselves to feel as if absolutely everything is important in life.
sentences.zh: 我们会让自己觉得，或者被灌输一种感觉，仿佛生活中的绝对一切都很重要。

sentences.en: Or as if we don't quite understand what's important and what's of value and what will benefit us always.
sentences.zh: 或者仿佛我们不太明白什么才是重要的、有价值的，以及什么总是对我们有利的。

sentences.en: And by thinking a little bit more deeply about priorities and prioritizing, I think we can begin to some extent, not entirely, of course,
sentences.zh: 通过更深入地思考优先事项和分清轻重缓急，我认为我们可以在一定程度上开始塑造我们所经历的现实，当然并非完全如此，

sentences.en: but to some extent to shape the reality that we walk through, both in terms of what we're doing in the world, but also in terms of how we feel internally.
sentences.zh: 但在某种程度上，无论是在我们世俗的行动方面，还是在我们內心的感受方面。

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 是的，完全同意。

sentences.en: And I have read your book and I've made some notes and I really like it.
sentences.zh: 我读了你的书，也做了一些笔记，我真的很喜欢。

sentences.en: It's really interesting food for thought.
sentences.zh: 这真的很耐人寻味，值得深思。

sentences.en: And there's a couple of kind of things that really struck me as I read it.
sentences.zh: 在我阅读时，有几件事情真的震撼了我。

sentences.en: And like there was a phrase, a wealth of information creates a poverty of attention.
sentences.zh: 比如有这样一句话：丰富的信息导致注意力的贫乏。

sentences.en: And it's like, yeah, it really does, doesn't it?
sentences.zh: 确实如此，不是吗？

sentences.en: Because it's like we're constantly just overstimulated and not really knowing where to attend to.
sentences.zh: 因为我们就像是不断地处于过度刺激之中，却真的不知道该把注意力放在哪里。

sentences.en: And as a result, maybe doing a pretty rubbish job of everything or most things, it's hard.
sentences.zh: 结果就是，可能把所有事情或者大多数事情都搞得一团糟，这很难。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And I mean, that's an old quote.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，那是一句老话了。

sentences.en: So that's from 1971, I think, the thinker wrote that.
sentences.zh: 那是1971年的话，我想，是某个思想家写的。

sentences.en: And God, like if they could see the world today, right?
sentences.zh: 天哪，如果他们能看到今天的世界，对吧？

sentences.en: The amount of information that's going on, this severe lack of resources that we have in terms of our attention and also how much money and effort goes into some of the,
sentences.zh: 信息量之大，我们在注意力方面严重缺乏资源，而且有多少金钱和精力被投入到其中，

sentences.en: drawing away some of that attention from us, you know, from social media companies.
sentences.zh: 把我们的注意力从我们身边拉开，你知道的，来自社交媒体公司。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And there's two points that are resonating with me from that is that even older, even further back, apparently the Romans had said, God, everything moves so quickly.
sentences.zh: 从那里面引起我共鸣的有两点，甚至更早，更遥远的时候，据说罗马人就说过，天哪，一切都变化得太快了。

sentences.en: And it's really hard to keep up with all this change and all this progress.
sentences.zh: 要跟上所有这些变化和所有的进步真的很难。

sentences.en: So this is not a new thing, you know, like humans have said this since humans existed, I guess, you know, since the wheel was invented.
sentences.zh: 所以这不是什么新鲜事，你知道的，人类自从有人类存在以来就一直在这么说，我想，自从发明了轮子以来。

sentences.en: Like, well, this is, this is wild.
sentences.zh: 就像，哇，这太疯狂了。

sentences.en: When I found that out, as I was doing the research for the book,
sentences.zh: 当我做这本书的研究发现这一点时，

sentences.en: I found that such a funny point because we do tend to think that we are so exceptional and that the way we think is so exceptional and so on.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这是一个非常有趣的观点，因为我们确实倾向于认为自己是如此杰出，我们的思维方式是如此杰出，诸如此类。

sentences.en: And it is, I think people will see this as a big era of change because it has been.
sentences.zh: 而且确实如此，我认为人们会把这视为一个巨大的变革时代，因为它的确是。

sentences.en: But yeah, that, you know, regardless of how humans have lived and how they've been operating, they've always felt that things are moving very faSt.
sentences.zh: 但是，不管人类如何生活，如何运作，他们总是觉得事情发展得非常快。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And then the other point is that people and corporations make big money from us having split focus or from us not paying attention to the things that maybe would make us more money or would help us to have better sleep.
sentences.zh: 另一个观点是，人们和大公司通过让我们分心，或者通过让我们不关注那些可能让我们赚更多钱或帮助我们睡得更好的事情，赚取了巨额财富。

sentences.en: And there was a company that you, you mentioned in your book.
sentences.zh: 书里提到了有一家公司。

sentences.en: Tell us, tell us about the Netflix analogy, what they'd said is their, their biggest competitor.
sentences.zh: 给我们讲讲，网飞的那个类比是怎么回事，他们说他们最大的竞争对手是什么。

sentences.en: Yeah, this is Reed Hastings, their CEO or was, I think it's still CEO now, was saying that their biggest competitor is sleep.
sentences.zh: 是的，这是里德·黑斯廷斯，他们的首席执行官，或者曾经是，我想现在还是首席执行官，他说他们最大的竞争对手是睡眠。

sentences.en: So it is when people, and I, I check this over and over again to, to check, did he really say this or is this, you know,
sentences.zh: 所以当人们——我一再核对这一点，来查证他是不是真的说过这话，还是说这只是

sentences.en: something the internet's made up and it does appear that it's an absolutely legitimate quote.
sentences.zh: 互联网虚构出来的东西——事实证明这绝对是一句名言。

sentences.en: Perhaps said slightly in jest, but as, I mean, as you know, as a clinical psychologist, often the things we say as a joke are the things we really mean.
sentences.zh: 也许说这话时略带玩笑意味，但是，正如你作为临床心理学家所知，我们开玩笑说的话往往就是我们的真心话。

sentences.en: If people slept less, then Netflix would get more watch hours and, you know, we'd have more money.
sentences.zh: 如果人们少睡一会儿，网飞就能获得更多的观看时长，你知道的，我们就能赚更多钱。

sentences.en: I should go to bed is the issue.
sentences.zh: 问题是我该去睡觉了。

sentences.en: Yeah, and it's that autoplay, isn't it, that comes up at the end after, you know, by the time you find your remote, sometimes, sometimes it started playing and then, you know,
sentences.zh: 是的，就是那个自动播放功能，你知道的，在节目结束时弹出来，等你找到遥控器的时候，有时候它已经开始播放了，然后，你知道的，

sentences.en: that sunk cost fallacy, oh, we might as well continue now, or we've already seen what happens next.
sentences.zh: 那种沉没成本谬误，哦，我们现在不妨继续看下去，或者我们已经知道了接下来会发生什么。

sentences.en: Like, yeah, that really blew my mind.
sentences.zh: 就像，哇，这真的让我大开眼界。

sentences.en: So, yeah, thinking about a couple of your chapters, if that's all right, to think about what might be really helpful for our listeners and our viewers.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，如果可以的话，我们来聊聊你的几个章节，想想什么对我们的听众和观众最有帮助。

sentences.en: I really like the stuff on procrastination, and that maybe speaks volumes about me.
sentences.zh: 我真的很喜欢关于拖延症的内容，这可能也说明了很多关于我自己的问题。

sentences.en: Why is procrastination so tricky for us as humans?
sentences.zh: 为什么拖延对我们人类来说这么棘手？

sentences.en: There's many reasons, but one of the most important, and I speak about quite a lot in the book, is we have, as I mean, again, as you well know, conflicting desires at all times.
sentences.zh: 原因有很多，但其中最重要的一点，也是我在书中经常谈到的，那就是我们——我的意思是，再次如你所知——随时都存在相互冲突的欲望。

sentences.en: And in terms of our brain and the way it operates, we have one desire, right,
sentences.zh: 就我们的大脑及其运作方式而言，我们有一种欲望，对吧，

sentences.en: to plan for the future and think of future me and anticipate and take the actions that are going to support our long-term objectives and aiMs.
sentences.zh: 为未来做计划，想着未来的自己，去预测并采取支持我们长期目标和目的的行动。

sentences.en: And then we have this other network of conversations in our brain that says, don't do that at all.
sentences.zh: 然后我们大脑中还有另一套对话网络，它说：千万别那么做。

sentences.en: You know what you should do.
sentences.zh: 你知道你应该做什么。

sentences.en: You should do exactly what you want right now, and that's going to be fucking amazing.
sentences.zh: 你应该立刻做你想做的事，那绝对会爽翻天。

sentences.en: So you should do what's going to feel really good now.
sentences.zh: 所以你应该做那些现在感觉真的很爽的事。

sentences.en: And in the book, I talk about that it's really just two quite opposing forces, perhaps like a tabloid versus a broadsheet editor, which feels very relevant at the moment,
sentences.zh: 我在书中谈到，这其实只是两种截然相反的力量，也许就像小报编辑与大报编辑的区别，这在目前看来非常贴切，

sentences.en: having just gone through the elections.
sentences.zh: 毕竟我们刚刚经历过选举。

sentences.en: And that these things fundamentally, these pathways in your brain fundamentally want different things, and that often the short-term wins out.
sentences.zh: 这些事情从根本上说，你大脑中的这些通路根本上想要的是不同的东西，而且通常是短期利益占了上风。

sentences.en: And when it comes to procrastination, that means that we put off perhaps doing the things now that we know we should do, and we seek instead to sort of feel better in the moment.
sentences.zh: 当涉及到拖延时，这意味着我们可能会推迟做那些我们知道现在应该做的事情，转而寻求在当下感觉更好。

sentences.en: And I think the big thing with procrastination is that everyone thinks it's a time management problem, and in part it is, absolutely, and it's also a habit of time management,
sentences.zh: 我认为关于拖延症最重要的一点是，大家都认为这是一个时间管理问题，部分而言确实如此，毫无疑问，这也是一种时间管理习惯的

sentences.en: mismanagement, let's say.
sentences.zh: 管理不善，我们这么说吧。

sentences.en: It's also completely and utterly fucking normal.
sentences.zh: 而且它完全彻底地他妈的正常。

sentences.en: So everyone procrastinates to some extent.
sentences.zh: 所以每个人在某种程度上都会拖延。

sentences.en: I procrastinate, and that's a whole chapter in the book.
sentences.zh: 我也会拖延，书里有一整章都在讲这个。

sentences.en: You know, we all procrastinate.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们都会拖延。

sentences.en: I know lots of people who write about it, and they still procrastinate.
sentences.zh: 我认识很多写这方面内容的人，他们照样拖延。

sentences.en: It's very normal, natural, and healthy to procrastinate a little bit.
sentences.zh: 拖延一点是非常正常、自然且健康的。

sentences.en: It's more when it starts impacting your life.
sentences.zh: 只有当它开始影响你的生活时才需要注意。

sentences.en: But we think it's a time management problem, and it is, but there's also this huge element of emotional management, and how we are, you know,
sentences.zh: 但我们认为这是一个时间管理问题，它确实是，但其中也有很大一部分是情绪管理，以及我们如何，你知道的，

sentences.en: if we don't want to do something by not doing it, we make ourselves feel better.
sentences.zh: 如果我们不想做某事，通过不做它，我们让自己感觉更好。

sentences.en: Because if the idea of doing something feels uncomfortable and feels hard, or feels like, say it's a big project, a big personal project that you've wanted to start for ages,
sentences.zh: 因为如果做某事的想法让人感到不舒服、困难，或者感觉——比方说这是一个你一直想开始的大项目，一个盛大的个人项目，

sentences.en: but you keep putting it off and putting it off, you know, perhaps there's that fear of failure.
sentences.zh: 但你一拖再拖，你知道，也许是出于对失败的恐惧。

sentences.en: Perhaps there's that perfectionism, perfectionist side of you that's scared to do something, scared you won't do it perfectly.
sentences.zh: 也许是你身上那完美主义的一面，害怕做某事，害怕自己做不完美。

sentences.en: And so you put it off.
sentences.zh: 所以你把它推迟了。

sentences.en: And so by putting it off, you are assuaging, is that the way you say it?
sentences.zh: 因此，通过推迟它，你是在减轻——是这么说的吗？

sentences.en: Assuaging?
sentences.zh: 减轻？

sentences.en: I pronounced that correctly.
sentences.zh: 我这个词发音对吧。

sentences.en: Those feelings, you know, you are making yourself feel better.
sentences.zh: 那些情绪，你知道的，你是在让自己感觉更好。

sentences.en: You are self-soothing.
sentences.zh: 你是在自我抚慰。

sentences.en: And we don't really acknowledge that enough when it comes to procrastination.
sentences.zh: 当谈到拖延时，我们并没有真正给予足够的认可。

sentences.en: We're just saying to people, you know, do X and Y.
sentences.zh: 我们只是对人们说，你知道的，去做A和B吧。

sentences.en: And of course, your work is so fundamentally incredible on this work, on this stuff,
sentences.zh: 当然，你在这些工作上的研究从根本上来说是如此不可思议，

sentences.en: because it's about getting people to dig in and say, okay, but what are the emotions that you're trying to avoid here?
sentences.zh: 因为它是关于引导人们深入挖掘并说：好吧，但是你在这里试图逃避的情绪是什么？

sentences.en: Yeah, and I love the idea.
sentences.zh: 是的，我太喜欢这个主意了。

sentences.en: So I've got Trello board, which is how I run everything.
sentences.zh: 我有Trello看板，我所有的事情都是通过它来管理的。

sentences.en: I run, aside from my clinical work with clients, I don't use Trello for that.
sentences.zh: 除了给客户做临床工作之外——我不会为那部分使用Trello。

sentences.en: But yeah, like all my podcast stuff, anything I've got to write, if it does, if it's not on Trello, it's not happening,
sentences.zh: 但是，是的，就像我的播客内容、我要写的东西，如果不记在Trello上，就什么都不会发生，

sentences.en: which is like a project management software for anyone's not familiar with that.
sentences.zh: 对于不太了解的人来说，这就像是一个项目管理软件。

sentences.en: But I will look at that when I've got some time.
sentences.zh: 但当我有些空闲时间时，我会看一眼它。

sentences.en: And I'll be like, what am I going to do now?
sentences.zh: 然后我会想：我现在要做什么呢？

sentences.en: And I'm not going to do that now.
sentences.zh: 我才不要现在做那个。

sentences.en: I'm going to do that now instead.
sentences.zh: 我要改做这个。

sentences.en: And in your book, you speak about something I think called affective forecasting, which is such a powerful and important idea.
sentences.zh: 在你的书里，你谈到了一种我称之为情感预测的东西，这是一个非常强大且重要的概念。

sentences.en: It's not something I'd heard of before, actually.
sentences.zh: 其实我以前没听说过这个。

sentences.en: But it's the idea that we'll look at what's ever on our to-do list and be like, well, I'll much prefer to do that a different day.
sentences.zh: 但它的意思是，我们会看看待办事项清单上的任何事情，然后想：嗯，我宁愿在别的日子做那件事。

sentences.en: Or we anticipate that it won't be as difficult on a different day.
sentences.zh: 或者我们预计在别的日子做它不会那么难。

sentences.en: When, of course, you know, largely, it's probably going to be the same as if we did it today.
sentences.zh: 而实际上，你知道，很大程度上，它可能跟我们今天做没什么两样。

sentences.en: Talk to us about that, Lily.
sentences.zh: 莉莉，跟我们聊聊这个吧。

sentences.en: Yeah, affective forecasting is so fascinating because our brain, as you said, essentially thinks to itself, present me doesn't want to do this.
sentences.zh: 是的，情感预测太迷人了，因为正如你所说，我们的大脑本质上在想：此时此地的“我”不想做这件事。

sentences.en: Present me right now in this moment doesn't.
sentences.zh: 此时此刻在这个瞬间的“我”不想做。

sentences.en: But next week, me is going to be a completely different kind of person.
sentences.zh: 但下周的“我”将会是一个完全不同的人。

sentences.en: And that person is really going to want to do it.
sentences.zh: 那个人会非常想做这件事。

sentences.en: And that's why, I mean, there's other reasons at play as well, but it's why we'll do things like
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么——我的意思是，还有其他原因在起作用，但这就是为什么我们会做出这样的行为，比如

sentences.en: not start a new habit on a Wednesday, but say, I'll wait till Monday because we have that idea.
sentences.zh: 不在周三开始一个新的习惯，而是说，我等到周因为我们有这种想法。

sentences.en: First of all, that future me is going to really want to do that and be really great at it.
sentences.zh: 首先，未来的“我”会非常想做这件事，而且会做得非常棒。

sentences.en: And the version of me on a Monday morning is going to be a different version than the me on a Wednesday morning as well.
sentences.zh: 而且周一早上的那个“我”，跟周三早上的那个“我”也会是不同版本的“我”。

sentences.en: But generally, you know, you are still you.
sentences.zh: 但总的来说，你知道，你依然是你。

sentences.en: I am still me in the same version.
sentences.zh: 我依然是我，还是同一个版本。

sentences.en: And so while you may have slightly more motivation at various different points, depending on other
sentences.zh: 所以，虽然你在不同的时间点可能会有稍微多一点的动力，取决于其他

sentences.en: circumstances and things that are going on in your brain or your life, having this idea that future you is going to do something a lot better or is going to want to do something is
sentences.zh: 环境以及你大脑中或生活中发生的事情，但抱着这种想法——即未来的你会把事情做得更好，或者会想要做某件事——

sentences.en: fundamentally wrong.
sentences.zh: 从根本上就是错的。

sentences.en: It really is.
sentences.zh: 真的是这样。

sentences.en: And I think there's knowing yourself.
sentences.zh: 我认为这就是了解你自己。

sentences.en: There's knowing if you're going out on a big weekend or you're going away with certain people that maybe don't schedule that for the Monday afterwards.
sentences.zh: 你要知道自己是否会在接下来的周末狂欢，或者是否要和某些人外出旅行，如果是的话，就不要把任务安排在随后的周一。

sentences.en: So there's knowing yourself, knowing what's reasonable.
sentences.zh: 所以这需要了解你自己，知道什么是合理的。

sentences.en: But also, yeah, like if I don't want to do this task now, I'm probably not going to want to do it next week either.
sentences.zh: 但同时，是的，如果我现在不想做这个任务，我下周可能也同样不想做。

sentences.en: So then it's how would we think about priorities?
sentences.zh: 那么，我们该如何看待优先级呢？

sentences.en: Is that really important to us?
sentences.zh: 这对我们真的那么重要吗？

sentences.en: Should we think about reprioritizing that so that we've got more on our plate of what what feels more abundantly within our comfortable wheelhouse or that we want to do?
sentences.zh: 我们是否应该考虑重新调整优先顺序，让我们手头上有更多更符合我们舒适区、或者我们真正想做的事情？

sentences.en: I mean, I guess life isn't always that simple, but is that like a clear communication if we're always like, no, no, don't want to do that.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，生活或许并非总是那么简单，但如果我们总是说“不，不，我不想做那个。我不想做那个”，这算是一种清晰的沟通吗？

sentences.en: Don't want to do that.
sentences.zh: 我不想做那个。

sentences.en: Well, I think that we put things off because it makes us feel better.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为我们推迟事情是因为这样做能让我们感觉好受一些。

sentences.en: But then if we actually think about it, a lot of the things that we put off, the pain and
sentences.zh: 但如果我们真正去思考，我们推迟的很多事情，其带来的痛苦和

sentences.en: stress that they cause us later down the line by putting them off is always actually stronger
sentences.zh: 推迟做事带来的压力，在日后往往总是比

sentences.en: and more pronounced than the relief, say, that we get from not doing it in the moment.
sentences.zh: 当下不做某事所获得的解脱感更强烈、

sentences.en: So I think that's one thing to start to think about for yourself in terms of how in terms of emotional management and how you are experiencing the world.
sentences.zh: 更加明显。所以我觉得，这是大家可以开始思考的第一件事，关于情绪管理，以及你是如何体验这个世界的。

sentences.en: Obviously, we're not going to do things perfectly.
sentences.zh: 显然，我们不可能把每件事都做得完美。

sentences.en: We never will.
sentences.zh: 永远都不可能。

sentences.en: But thinking of this in terms of, well, A, if this is really important to me, how can I make this more important?
sentences.zh: 但我们可以换个角度来想，A，如果这件事对我很重要，我该如何让它显得更重要？

sentences.en: How can I make it so that I act on it?
sentences.zh: 我该如何让自己去付诸行动？

sentences.en: What are the barriers that I need to move through?
sentences.zh: 我需要克服哪些阻碍？

sentences.en: Say it's a big personal project we're talking about at this point.
sentences.zh: 比方说，我们现在讨论的是一个重大的个人项目。

sentences.en: What are the what are the barriers that I need to move through?
sentences.zh: 我需要克服哪些阻碍？

sentences.en: Is it that I need to work on my fear of failure?
sentences.zh: 我是需要克服对失败的恐惧吗？

sentences.en: Is it that I need to work maybe with a partner, you know, not on the project itself, but on just getting things done?
sentences.zh: 我是不是需要和一个伙伴合作——你知道的，不是合作项目本身，而是一起把事情推进下去？

sentences.en: So we call it body doubling in coaching, where you just do something with someone else instead just to get you there.
sentences.zh: 所以在教练技术中，我们称之为“搭伴并行”（body doubling），就是你和另一个人一起做某事，只是为了督促自己开始。

sentences.en: And then sometimes that action can lead to that motivation and that can create some momentum.
sentences.zh: 有时这种行动能够带来动力，进而产生一些势头。

sentences.en: Do I need to?
sentences.zh: 我需要这样做吗？

sentences.en: And then if it's something, say, your taxes or something that you put off, so it's not maybe a big, important project, but something that's more urgent, thinking about, OK, but
sentences.zh: 如果这是一件你一直拖延的事情，比如报税或者别的什么，它也许不是一个重大且重要的项目，但却更加紧急，你可以思考：好的，但是

sentences.en: how can I break this down?
sentences.zh: 我该如何把任务拆解开来？

sentences.en: Because it's a very big task and it feels intimidating and say, like, really not one with numbers.
sentences.zh: 因为这是一个非常大的任务，让人望而生畏，而且假如你确实不擅长数字的话。

sentences.en: Then it's going to feel very intimidating to your brain and your brain is going to shy away from that because one of your brain's main priorities, aside from staying alive,
sentences.zh: 那么你的大脑就会对它感到非常畏惧，大脑也会选择退缩，因为大脑的核心优先级之一——除了维持生存之外

sentences.en: is conserving energy because that helps it stay alive.
sentences.zh: 就是保存能量，因为这有助于维持生存。

sentences.en: So tasks that take a lot of effort use up a lot of energy.
sentences.zh: 所以需要付出巨大努力的任务会消耗大量能量。

sentences.en: And so sometimes your brain will shy away from that, particularly if you have habits around shying away from things which are difficult.
sentences.zh: 因此，有时候你的大脑会对此退缩，特别是当你习惯于逃避困难的事情时。

sentences.en: So it's about how can you break things down and make them more manageable for your brain?
sentences.zh: 所以关键在于，你如何将事情拆解，让它们对你的大脑来说更容易应对？

sentences.en: How can you make it so that you don't get that visceral reaction of like, absolutely not.
sentences.zh: 你该如何避免那种“绝对不要、

sentences.en: Let me do something else.
sentences.zh: 让我去做点别的吧”的本能抗拒？

sentences.en: I'm going to ignore that thing on the to-do list until it's so big that it's actually causing a lot of stress in my life.
sentences.zh: 我打算一直无视待办清单上的那件事，直到它变得大到真的开始给我的生活带来巨大压力。

sentences.en: Yeah, because our brains are clever things.
sentences.zh: 是的，因为我们的大脑很聪明。

sentences.en: You know, they're trying to always be averse to pain and stress and move away from that.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，它们总是试图抗拒痛苦和压力，并远离这些东西。

sentences.en: And so if it feels really big and really awful, it makes sense that we're going to look for easier options.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果事情感觉非常重大且糟糕，我们会去寻找更轻松的选择，这也就合乎情理了。

sentences.en: But yeah, like I like the idea of in the book that you talk about, maybe don't do the whole thing.
sentences.zh: 但是，对，就像我很喜欢你在书中提到的那个观点，也许不要把整件事全做完。

sentences.en: You know, start 10 minutes just and then because when we do that, I mean, how many times have we done something where we're like, oh, actually, it wasn't that bad.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，先开始10分钟，然后——因为当我们这样做时，我是说，有多少次我们做完之后会觉得：哦，其实没那么糟。

sentences.en: Yeah, it wasn't that bad.
sentences.zh: 对，其实没那么糟。

sentences.en: It wasn't that bad.
sentences.zh: 其实没那么糟。

sentences.en: So just make a start like and then you might find that it kind of flows more easily.
sentences.zh: 所以只要开始行动就行了，接着你可能会发现事情进展得更顺畅了。

sentences.en: And then if it doesn't, at least you've made a start as well.
sentences.zh: 如果还是不行，至少你也已经迈出了第一步。

sentences.en: And then you know that actually it is quite a challenging task.
sentences.zh: 而且你也会明白，这其实真的是一项具有挑战性的任务。

sentences.en: And so you might need more time than you thought you did versus if you leave it till the last minute you start it, it's actually quite hard.
sentences.zh: 因此，你可能需要比想象中更多的时间，这和留到最后一分钟才开始、结果发现其实很难的情况完全不同。

sentences.en: And then you're a bit fucked because you don't actually have the time to do the project or whatever it is.
sentences.zh: 然后你就有点完蛋了，因为你根本没有时间来完成这个项目或别的什么。

sentences.en: Was it for the procrastination topic that you spoke about the four quadrants and breaking things up?
sentences.zh: 你讲到四个象限和任务拆解时，是不是为了谈论拖延这个话题？

sentences.en: Guide us through that.
sentences.zh: 给我们讲解一下吧。

sentences.en: So that's called the Eisenhower matrix or the priorities matrix, which is just very convenient for me as opposed to something I named.
sentences.zh: 这被称为艾森豪威尔矩阵或优先级矩阵，对我来说它只是用起来很方便，并不是我发明的东西。

sentences.en: And it's you divide your tasks from your to do liSt.
sentences.zh: 具体做法是把待办清单上的任务进行分类。

sentences.en: And that might be like your short term daily to do list, but maybe your greater to do list as well in terms of the things you want to do with your, with your life.
sentences.zh: 这既可以是你的短期每日待办清单，也可以是你关于人生规划的宏大待办清单。

sentences.en: And you sort them into four quadrants according to whether something is urgent and important, whether something is not urgent, but still important, whether something is urgent, but
sentences.zh: 你根据任务的紧急且重要程度、不紧急但重要程度、紧急但

sentences.en: not important, or whether something is not urgent and not important.
sentences.zh: 不重要程度，或者不紧急也不重要程度，将它们归入四个象限。

sentences.en: And then you can sort of work through and see, you know, if something is urgent and important, you need to do that thing right now.
sentences.zh: 然后你就可以进行梳理，看一看：如果一件事既紧急又重要，你必须立刻去做。

sentences.en: So that's one going to be on the list of things you absolutely shouldn't put off.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是绝对不能拖延的事项之一。

sentences.en: If something is not urgent and not important, then there's the question of like, why is it on there in the first place?
sentences.zh: 如果一件事既不紧急也不重要，那么就会产生这样的疑问：它为什么会出现在清单上？

sentences.en: And then you've got the tasks which maybe have less urgency, but are really important.
sentences.zh: 接下来是那些或许没那么紧急、但真的很重要的任务。

sentences.en: And that could be where there's personal project type things fall.
sentences.zh: 个人项目之类的东西通常就属于这一类。

sentences.en: And those are the things that always get shoved down the list and shoved down the list because they're not urgent, but they might be really important to you.
sentences.zh: 这些事情总是被一推再推、一推再推，因为它们不紧急，但对你而言可能真的很重要。

sentences.en: And then again, that question from before of how can you bring more urgency to it so that, you know, you can do the things, you can prioritize the projects and things that
sentences.zh: 这就又回到了之前的问题：你该如何为它注入更多紧迫感，以便你能去完成那些项目，并优先处理那些

sentences.en: are really, truly important to you.
sentences.zh: 对你真正极其重要的事情？

sentences.en: And then when you think about the other quadrant, which is maybe not so grandly important, but quite urgent.
sentences.zh: 再来看看另一个象限，可能没有那么宏大重要，但却相当紧急。

sentences.en: So that might be like admin-y stuff that for those, I always recommend that instead of doing it one by one, so that's admin or bills or whatever, rather than doing it immediately
sentences.zh: 比如处理行政事务之类的琐事。对于这些，我给出的建议是：与其一项一项地去办（比如行政事务或账单之类），不如

sentences.en: when it comes in, you can group them together and do them once a week or twice a week or once a day, depending on the type of work and life you have.
sentences.zh: 在它们刚出现时并不立刻处理，而是把它们集中起来，每周、每半周或每天集中处理一次，这取决于你的工作和生活类型。

sentences.en: And that you're not constantly drawing from your attention and energy bank that you've got in your head.
sentences.zh: 这样你就不会不断透支你脑海中的注意力与能量银行。

sentences.en: And you can use some of your focus and attention for the more important things.
sentences.zh: 你可以把更多的注意力和专注力留给更重要的事情。

sentences.en: And then you can group those little things together and you'll get all those dopamine hits.
sentences.zh: 然后把这些小事集中处理，你就会收获满满的的多巴胺。

sentences.en: You know, the reason we like doing those little things quickly is because when you take something off your to-do list, you get a dopamine hit in your brain.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我们喜欢快速处理这些小事的原因是，每当你在待办清单上划掉一项，你的大脑就会获得一次多巴胺奖励。

sentences.en: Your brain likes that chemical.
sentences.zh: 你的大脑喜欢这种化学物质。

sentences.en: And so it's always going to seek that out and it's going to seek out those small hits.
sentences.zh: 所以它会不断寻求这种刺激，去寻找那些小小的多巴胺奖励。

sentences.en: And so what you want to do is kind of fight against that slightly and group them together.
sentences.zh: 因此，你需要做的是稍微对抗一下这种本能，把这些琐事集中起来。

sentences.en: So you still get that hit, but you also wade through the discomfort of maybe doing the bigger
sentences.zh: 这样你既能获得那种快感，同时也能去克服处理那些更重大

sentences.en: tasks that need to be done and keeping your focus and attention on them rather than let it be split the whole time by smaller little things.
sentences.zh: 且必须完成的任务所带来的不适感，把注意力和专注力保持在这些大事上，而不是让它们一直被那些鸡毛蒜皮的小事分散。

sentences.en: And that's, you know, put your phone on, do not disturb when you're working so that you're not constantly, oh, I better reply to that WhatsApp from my kid's school quickly
sentences.zh: 这就好比，工作时把手机调到“请勿打扰”模式，这样你就不会总是想着：哦，我得赶紧回复一下我孩子学校发来的WhatsApp消息

sentences.en: and so on.
sentences.zh: 诸如此类。

sentences.en: You know, you want the urgent stuff, the truly urgent stuff to get through.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，你需要让紧急的事情、真正紧急的事情顺利通过。

sentences.en: But it's also a really big point of remembering.
sentences.zh: 但这里还有一个非常重要需要铭记的点。

sentences.en: So I'm going on a bit now of remembering that other people's urgent is not your urgent.
sentences.zh: ——我这会儿有点扯远了——要记住：别人的紧急并不是你的紧急。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's so important, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 对，这太重要了，不是吗？

sentences.en: It's so important and we so often forget it.
sentences.zh: 这真的太重要了，而我们却经常忘记这一点。

sentences.en: And I do the same, you know, just and I'm not saying to anyone listening that, you know, your boss says something's urgent and you decide it's not, don't, like, you'll probably
sentences.zh: 我自己也会犯同样的错误，我并不是在对任何听众说，如果你们的老板说某事很紧急而你却觉得不紧急，就直接无视——如果你那样做的话，可能

sentences.en: just lose your job after a while if you, if you work like that.
sentences.zh: 过不了多久就会丢掉工作。

sentences.en: However, just thinking, you know, that it's, everyone's the main character in their life
sentences.zh: 然而，只要转念一想：每个人都是自己生活中的主角，

sentences.en: and everyone is moving through assuming that people are going to move and respond, hopefully move and respond in the ways that they want.
sentences.zh: 每个人都在前行，并默认别人会按照他们希望的方式去行动和回应、最好是如他们所愿地行动和回应。

sentences.en: And it's our job sometimes to make sure that we are not sacrificing who we are to those bigger
sentences.zh: 而我们的工作，有时就是确保我们不会为了迎合那些更有气场、更有个性

sentences.en: personalities or bigger characters who maybe play, it feels like place more importance on stuff.
sentences.zh: 并且似乎把某些事情看得更重的人，而牺牲了真正的自我。

sentences.en: And so we're understanding, you know what, it's not urgent that I respond to that email from that particular colleague today.
sentences.zh: 所以我们要明白，你知道吗，今天不回复那位特定同事的电子邮件并不紧急。

sentences.en: Okay, I can do that until tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 没关系，我可以拖到明天再处理。

sentences.en: That is not urgent on my plate and I need to prioritise and think what is because otherwise
sentences.zh: 这件事在我的待办日程里并不紧急，我需要分清轻重缓急，思考真正重要的是什么，否则

sentences.en: you're always going to be responding to other people's demands and timetables and ways of being rather than understanding what's truly important to you and how you're going to move
sentences.zh: 你将永远都在疲于应付别人的要求、时间表和生活方式，而不是去弄清楚到底什么对你真正重要、你又该如何推动

sentences.en: your own life forward.
sentences.zh: 自己的人生向前发展。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think before I became a parent, I was very much able to flex and probably just create
sentences.zh: 是的，我想在我成为父母之前，我非常能够灵活变通，可能只是在一天当中挤出

sentences.en: more time in my day or, or maybe have shorter breaks to be able to get other people's changing priorities flexed for.
sentences.zh: 更多时间，或者缩短休息时间，以便去适应其他人不断变化的需求。

sentences.en: So yeah, your boss comes along, your manager wants something done.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，老板走过来，经理希望完成某项工作。

sentences.en: And I think certainly now I'm a parent, I can't always just do that.
sentences.zh: 我想毫无疑问，现在我成为了父母，我不能总是那样做了。

sentences.en: Um,
sentences.zh: 嗯，

sentences.en: uh, and so I think something can be really powerful is to say, actually, yeah, if this is urgent and this is important, you can be like to your manager or your boss, can you
sentences.zh: 所以我觉得有一个非常有力的方法，就是直接跟你的经理或老板说：事实上，如果这件事既紧急又重要，你能

sentences.en: help me look at all the other bits I've already got to work out maybe what doesn't need to be done as quickly today by this week?
sentences.zh: 帮我看看手头上其他的活儿吗，我们来评估一下，本周内有哪些事情其实没必要赶得那么急？

sentences.en: Because I definitely can do that, but I can't then do all these other things as well, because that would be a wellbeing detriment to yourself.
sentences.zh: 因为这件事我绝对可以做，但我无法同时搞定所有其他的事情，因为那会对你的身心健康造成损害。

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 对，绝对是这样。

sentences.en: So if you try to never compare, I think you just fail slightly because we are, I don't

sentences.en: want to say, we're biologically wired to compare, to want to understand how we are doing compared to the people around us.

sentences.en: Our brains develop within social conditions and around and in response to other people and what they were doing in life.
sentences.zh: 所以这种特质已经深深地、深深地烙印在我们的基因里。

sentences.en: So that is really, really ingrained in us.
sentences.zh: 试图不去进行比较，有点像试图压抑任何一种情绪。

sentences.en: And trying to not do it is a little bit like trying to push away any feeling.

sentences.en: You know, if you push away some sadness, it's going to come up in some weird and not wonderful ways later down the line.
sentences.zh: 我觉得比较也是一样，我们需要接纳它，我们需要对自己说：“我天生就是个爱比较的生物。”

sentences.en: And I think it's similar with comparison, that we need to accept it, that we need to say, you know, I am a comparative creature by nature.
sentences.zh: 有些人可能比其他人更严重。

sentences.en: Some people be more so than others.
sentences.zh: 那么我该如何承认这就是我的天性、是我的一部分，并尽最大努力去引导它，让它不会对我的自我认同、自我价值感以及

sentences.zh: 我在这世上为人处世的方式产生过于负面的影响？

sentences.en: way that I navigate my way through this world.

sentences.en: And I think there are many tools that we can use there where we can interrupt our brain

sentences.en: pattern, you know, our thought patterns and what we're saying to ourselves around comparison.

sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，十有八九，百分之九十九的时候，答案都是不，我其实并不想要那样。

sentences.zh: 然后要想清楚，好吧，既然我想要其中的一部分，那么更深一层的东西又是什么呢？

sentences.zh: 我真的想要那个手袋吗？

sentences.en: But before that arrives, if that arrives, we have to think like, how can I better support myself and how can I look a little bit deeper behind some of those feelings of like envy

sentences.zh: 然后说，好吧，我怎么才能把它转化成一种能支持我自己的方式，让我

sentences.en: And then when it comes to social media, I strongly, strongly recommend if you're in that

sentences.zh: 莉莉，我真的很喜欢你的书。

sentences.en: So it's called Prioritise This and it's by Lily Silverton.
sentences.zh: 这本书叫《优先考虑这个》（Prioritise This），作者是莉莉·西尔弗顿。

sentences.en: I'm assuming it can be accessed wherever people get their books.
sentences.zh: 我想大家在买书的地方都能买到吧？

sentences.en: Is it also an audio book?
sentences.zh: 它也有有声书吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: It's also an audio book.
sentences.zh: 它也有有声书。

sentences.en: Um, if you didn't mind my voice today, then I'm the one that reads it.
sentences.zh: 嗯，如果你今天不介意我的声音的话，那这本书就是我读的。

sentences.en: If you did, then don't get the audio.
sentences.zh: 如果你介意，那就别买有声书了。

sentences.en: It's not a good idea.
sentences.zh: 那不是个好主意。

sentences.en: And yeah, it's all around how to prioritise more helpful ways of thinking or behaving in this modern world, whilst also
sentences.zh: 是的，这本书主要讲的是在这个现代世界中，如何优先采取更有帮助的思维或行为方式，同时

sentences.en: recognising, I guess, that the world will continue to be itself.
sentences.zh: 我也意识到，这个世界还会一如既往地运转下去。

sentences.en: So what I found with a lot of self-help books is that they promise the absolute world and they promise that if you just read this book, then life is going to be perfect.
sentences.zh: 所以我发现很多自助书都有一个问题，它们承诺了整个世界，承诺只要你读了这本书，生活就会变得十全十美。

sentences.en: And you know, this is how it's going to be from now on.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，从今以后生活就会变成这样。

sentences.en: And I fundamentally and strongly disagree with that.
sentences.zh: 但我从根本上强烈反对这种说法。

sentences.en: And so I was trying very much to offer a book that provides the kind of support that goes alongside, you know, incredible psychology work that you guys
sentences.zh: 所以我非常努力地想要提供这样一本书，它所提供的支持可以与你们

sentences.en: do, but that really meets people where they're at in their lives and supports them that way.
sentences.zh: 所做的了不起的心理学工作相辅相成，但它真正能够走进人们的生活，并在那里为他们提供支持。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I did really enjoy it.
sentences.zh: 我真的很喜欢它。

sentences.en: So I will definitely leave your review as well.
sentences.zh: 所以我一定会为它写一篇书评的。

sentences.en: Can people come and follow you on Instagram, Lily?
sentences.zh: 大家可以去Instagram上关注你吗，莉莉？

sentences.en: Is that the best place to keep up with you and your work?
sentences.zh: 那是了解你和你工作最新动态的最佳平台吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, I'm on Lily underscore Silverton on Instagram.
sentences.zh: 对，我在Instagram上的账号是Lily underscore Silverton（Lily_Silverton）。

sentences.en: And I do a bunch of mindset-y stuff, type stuff on there.
sentences.zh: 我在上面发很多关于思维模式之类的内容。

sentences.en: And then I also have a newsletter on Substack, which is the same name as the book is called Prioritise This.
sentences.zh: 另外我在Substack上也有一份通讯，名字和书名一样，叫《优先考虑这个》（Prioritise This）。

sentences.en: Amazing.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: I'll pop all the links in the description and in the show notes.
sentences.zh: 我会把所有的链接都放在简介和节目文稿里。

sentences.en: But thank you so much for your time.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢你抽出时间。

sentences.en: And thank you for writing this book.
sentences.zh: 也谢谢你写了这本书。

sentences.en: As I said, I did really enjoy it.
sentences.zh: 正如我所说，我真的很喜欢它。

sentences.en: And yeah, people can find all the details in the description.
sentences.zh: 是的，大家可以在简介里找到所有的详细信息。

sentences.en: Thanks again for your time, Lily.
sentences.zh: 莉莉，再次感谢你抽出时间。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: Thanks so much for your time in watching or listening to this episode.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢大家收看或收听本期节目。

sentences.en: If it's resonated with you, please do share it to your socials, tag myself, tag Lily in socials.
sentences.zh: 如果这引发了你的共鸣，请把它分享到你的社交媒体上，并@我和莉莉。

sentences.en: We love to hear from you.
sentences.zh: 我们很乐意听到你的反馈。

sentences.en: And this really does help the show to grow.
sentences.zh: 这确实对节目的成长很有帮助。

sentences.en: I am Dr. Marianne Trent everywhere.
sentences.zh: 我到处都是“玛丽安·特伦特博士”（Dr. Marianne Trent）。

sentences.en: So do come and connect and let me know if you've got any ideas for future guests or episodes too.
sentences.zh: 所以快来和联系我吧，如果你对未来的嘉宾或节目有什么想法，也请告诉我。

sentences.en: Lily and I spoke off camera about both having experienced losing our fathers, especially losing our fathers when we're pregnant with our youngest children.
sentences.zh: 我和莉莉在镜头之外聊过，我们都有过失去父亲的经历，尤其是怀着最小的孩子时失去了父亲。

sentences.en: Not an easy thing to do at all.
sentences.zh: 这绝对不是一件容易的事。

sentences.en: If you have experience of grief or want to understand someone who might be grieving, please do also bear in mind the Grief Collective book.
sentences.zh: 如果你有悲伤的经历，或者想理解一个可能正在经历悲伤的人，请务必关注《悲伤合集》（Grief Collective）这本书。

sentences.en: If you're a big fan of psychology, actually, I think you'll also really like the companion podcast series called Inner Work.
sentences.zh: 如果你是心理学的超级粉丝，其实我觉得你也会非常喜欢我们的姊妹播客系列《内心工作》（Inner Work）。

sentences.en: They're all exclusive solo episodes with me.
sentences.zh: 里面全部都是由我主讲的独家单人节目。

sentences.en: And I explore some of the real life thoughts, reflections, feelings, insights about what it's like to be a psychologist, what it's like for this
sentences.zh: 我在节目中探讨了一些真实的想法、反思、感受和见解，关于身为心理学家是什么体验，关于这些

sentences.en: to crop up in my life, in my work, in my day to day and the reflections, insights and kind of growth moments that I have as a human and as a professional.
sentences.zh: 如何在我的生活、工作和日常中涌现，以及作为一个人和一个专业人士，我所拥有的反思、见解和成长时刻。

sentences.en: I think you'll love it.
sentences.zh: 我想你会爱上它的。

sentences.en: You can come and grab a free three-day trial on Apple Podcasts.
sentences.zh: 你可以在苹果播客（Apple Podcasts）上免费试用三天。

sentences.en: You can also grab a trial on Patreon and you can subscribe on YouTube and directly on Captivate.
sentences.zh: 你也可以在Patreon上试用，还可以在YouTube以及Captivate上直接订阅。

sentences.en: Psychologists, what if you could earn money beyond trading your time for money?
sentences.zh: 心理学家们，如果你们除了用时间换金钱之外还能赚钱，会怎么样呢？

sentences.en: I'm Dr. Marianne Trent, clinical psychologist, and I've been developing passive and recurring income streams since 2019.
sentences.zh: 我是玛丽安·特伦特博士，临床心理学家，自2019年以来，我一直在开发被动和经常性收入流。

sentences.en: I have some exciting news.
sentences.zh: 我有一个激动人心的消息要宣布。

sentences.en: Sophie Foote's one-to-many program is now open for enrolment.
sentences.zh: 苏菲·福特（Sophie Foote）的一对多项目现已开放报名。

sentences.en: It's designed to help you turn your expertise into scalable offers like courses, memberships and digital products.
sentences.zh: 它旨在帮助你将专业知识转化为可规模化的产品，比如课程、会员资格和数字产品。

sentences.en: I completed the program myself in 2022 and have since supported two cohorts of psychologists through their journeys too.
sentences.zh: 我本人于2022年完成了这个项目，此后也一直支持两期心理学家走过他们的成长旅程。

sentences.en: And if you join through my affiliate link, you'll receive Sophie's bonuses plus my own exclusive support package at no extra coSt.
sentences.zh: 如果你通过我的专属联盟链接加入，你将获得苏菲的额外福利以及我个人的独家支持套餐，无需支付额外费用。

sentences.en: That includes six months of WhatsApp support, four group masterminds, masterclasses, personalized guidance, a Fortnum and Mason treat and a time-limited one-to-one coaching bonus.
sentences.zh: 其中包括六个月的WhatsApp支持、四次小组大师班、大师课、个性化指导、一份福特姆与梅森（Fortnum & Mason）礼品以及限时的一对一教练指导福利。

sentences.en: Enrolment closes on Monday the 16th of November at 10pm.
sentences.zh: 报名将于11月16日（星期一）晚上10点截止。

sentences.en: Find out more via my bonus page linked in the description.
sentences.zh: 请通过简介中链接的我的福利页面了解更多信息。

sentences.en: And remember, you must purchase through my link to receive my bonuses.
sentences.zh: 请记住，你必须通过我的链接购买才能获得我的福利。

sentences.en: I'm here if you have any questions.
sentences.zh: 如果你有任何问题，我随时都在。
